sanskrit: ā te manaś cakṣuṣyam ā te hṛdayyaṃ dade | padoṣ ṭe padyam ā dade yathā tiṣṭhāsi me vaśe ||
english: I seize what is eye-dear in your mind, I seize what is heart-dear in you; I seize what is foot-dear in your feet — so that you shall stand under my command.

sanskrit: vāñcha me pādau tanvaṃ vāñchākṣyau vāñcha sakthyau | akṣyau vṛṣaṇyantyāḥ keśā oṣṭhau māṃ te kāmena śuṣyatām ||
english: Yearn for my feet, yearn for my body, yearn for my eyes, yearn for my thighs; may your eyes, the hair of the wanton one, and your lips wither with longing for me.

sanskrit: mayi tvā doṣaṇiśliṣaṃ kṛṇomi hṛdayaśliṣam | yathā mama kratāv aso mamāsaś ced asīd api ||
english: I make you cling to my arms, cling to my heart — so that you shall be in my will, and as if you had always already been mine.

sanskrit: yāsāṃ nābhir ārehaṇaṃ hṛdi saṃvananaṃ kṛtam | gāvo ghṛtasya mātaro amūṃ saṃ vānayantu me ||
english: Those [cows] whose navel is the mounting-place, in whose heart the charm of conciliation is wrought — the cows, mothers of ghee, shall draw that woman together to me.

sanskrit: mahyaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī mahyaṃ devī sarasvatī | mahyaṃ tvendraś cāgniś ca- -ahorātre ni yacchatām ||
english: May Dyāvāpṛthivī yield you to me; may the divine Sarasvatī yield you to me; may Indra and Agni together, and Day-and-Night, deliver you to me.

sanskrit: tūli mūly arjuni punar vo yantu yātavaḥ punar jūtiḥ kimīdinīḥ | yasya stha tam atta yo vaḥ prāhait tam atta svā māṃsāny atta ||
english: O Tūlī, O Mūlī, O Arjunī — let the demons return to you, let the swift-rushing Kimīdinīs return; devour him whose creatures you are, devour him who sent you forth, devour your own flesh.
The man-eaters, the devourers, [return to him who unleashed them] — devour him whose creatures you are, devour him who sent you forth, devour your own flesh.
The worm-ridden ones, the foul-drinking ones, [return to him who unleashed them] — devour him whose creatures you are, devour him who sent you forth, devour your own flesh.
The stealers of prosperity, the stealers of vital sap, [return to him who unleashed them] — devour him whose creatures you are, devour him who sent you forth, devour your own flesh.

sanskrit: vātajūte manojavaḥ punar vo yantu yātavaḥ punar jūtiḥ kimīdinīḥ | yasya stha tam atta yo vaḥ prāhait tam atta svā māṃsāny atta ||
english: Wind-impelled, swift as thought — let the demons return to you, let the swift-rushing Kimīdinīs return; devour him whose creatures you are, devour him who sent you forth, devour your own flesh.
